The build passed. It failed at the permission check in CI, which worked as intended. Your own `AndroidManifest.xml` doesn't ask for `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`. A library the app depends on indirectly adds it when Android merges all the manifests into the final APK. It didn't show up locally because none of the commands you ran inspect the APK's permissions with `aapt2`. `pr-check.yml` runs the same check on the debug APK, so it would fail too.

**Fix:** your manifest now strips the network permissions no matter which library adds them. This applies to both debug and release builds, so both CI workflows should pass. I haven't run the build here, so the next CI run is the real test. It's safe because the app never calls Android's connectivity APIs.

Two files changed, nothing to delete:

**`app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`**
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools">

    <!-- Strip network permissions that transitive AndroidX libraries merge in; the app is fully offline. -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" tools:node="remove" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE" tools:node="remove" />

    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
```

**`README.md`**: only the "100% Offline & Private" line changed. It now says all three permissions are stripped and that CI fails if any of them come back. The full file is in the attachment above.

To check locally before pushing:
```bash
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug && "$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/37.0.0/aapt2" dump permissions app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```
To see which library added the permission, look in `app/build/outputs/logs/manifest-merger-*-report.txt`.
